direct: Drupal says the core access bypass CVE-2026-136716 (SA-CORE-2026-019) is exploited in the wild; fixed in 10.6.23, 11.3.23 and 11.4.14. It comes a week after SA-CORE-2026-017 (install.php reinstall), exploited from Nov 19 and in CISA KEV since Nov 24.
downstream: Drupal says sites whose installer stayed reachable after 017 may already be compromised, so updating now does not clean a site that was taken over (stated).
Government, university and media sites run Drupal widely; defacement, data theft or use as phishing hosts are likely follow-ons (inference).
watch_for: A CISA KEV entry for CVE-2026-136716
Unexpected admin accounts or a reinstalled site
Mass-scanning reports for install.php and the 019 path
who_should_care: Drupal site owners and hosting providers

direct: Secutec and SOCRadar say an operator (BabidiGhost) used a DeepSeek-driven agent to take identity data of about 1.2 million people in 82 Flemish municipalities from a service provider's server; the CCB was told on Nov 16 and a prosecutor is investigating.
downstream: Residents of the 82 municipalities can expect targeted phishing using their identity data (inference).
SOCRadar says the same operator also went after European banks, insurers and payment providers, so other victims may follow (stated by SOCRadar; victims not named).
Shows a low-skill operator reaching large data sets with an AI agent, as the Swiss NCSC also reports (inference from both).
watch_for: CCB confirmation of scope
Named victims from SOCRadar's list
Data offered for sale
who_should_care: Belgian municipalities and their IT providers

direct: Palo Alto Networks says Fragnesia (CVE-2026-46300), a Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw, was exploited against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet, after attackers first exploited PHP2Shell; fixed PAN-OS builds are listed in PAN-SA-2026-0015.
downstream: PHP2Shell was already used to root and in some cases wipe unpatched Check Point gateways from Oct 30, so the same entry point now reaches two firewall vendors (stated by each vendor).
A firewall rooted through its management interface can expose VPN credentials, configuration and traffic policy for the whole network (our inference from how the product works).
Any other appliance that bundles PHP with the PHP2Shell or phpAfterShell flaws may be reachable the same way (inference; no other vendor has said so).
watch_for: A CISA KEV entry for CVE-2026-46300
Other appliance vendors naming PHP2Shell or phpAfterShell in their products
Unexpected admin sessions or files on PAN-OS management interfaces
Victim reports or counts from Palo Alto Networks
who_should_care: Palo Alto Networks customers with management interfaces reachable from the internet

direct: PLAID suspended all KARTE services after a vulnerability was exploited on Nov 13; its own account emails and contacts were taken, and customer data of several hundred companies was affected in each data category. It plans a phased restart in mid-January 2027.
downstream: Customers report the scale: DHC about 19.11 million records, ZOZO about 15.18 million, SMBC up to about 14 million, Marui about 8.83 million, MUFG Bank about 6.5 million; this week JCB (up to about 150,000 management codes), Shikoku Bank's Mikatano and GO added notices.

Leaked profiles (names, emails, dates of birth, purchase attributes, and for some Marui card members income) make convincing phishing in Japanese; integration credentials held by the service may open customers' own systems.
Companies that ended their KARTE contract are included, so former customers should check too.
watch_for: Further KARTE customers announcing leaks
Phishing that uses shop names, member IDs and dates of birth
Use of integration keys connected to KARTE
Regulator action by Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission

direct: Binance says about $6.34 billion was affected and about $2.85 billion frozen or intercepted; the way in was malware in a coding assignment given to an engineer through a recruitment platform. The FBI attributes the theft to North Korea.
downstream: Fake job tests aimed at developers are a proven route to exchange infrastructure; Socket reports the same lure in NuGet packages (no stated link).
UK FCA reportedly presses ahead with DeFi authorization rules, citing the theft (stated).
Laundering through coinjoin and DeFi continues, and US forfeiture covers over $1.1 billion (stated).
watch_for: More seizures or freezes
Recruiter approaches with take-home coding tests
Other exchanges disclosing the same lure

direct: 1Password says an attacker used an employee's corporate GitHub account to push malicious code to backend services, which downloaded account records for a subset of users (names, emails, tokens in some invitation and recovery emails); source code was copied. Vaults were not affected, it says.
downstream: Affected users may get phishing that quotes real account details or recovery flows (inference).
Copied source code may be studied for flaws (inference).
Todoist reported a stolen development credential reaching production the day before; no link is stated.
watch_for: 1Password's final count and token revocations
Phishing posing as 1Password recovery
Other firms reporting GitHub account takeover

direct: Microsoft says China-linked Salt Typhoon and Crystal Typhoon use the ARTEX AI attack framework and that North Korean and Chinese groups have adopted it; its best signal is a large volume of anomalous traffic from one source.
downstream: State groups with telecom focus (Salt Typhoon) can now scan and exploit at agent speed (inference).
Shadowserver counts about 4,200 exposed AI attack-framework instances, mostly ARTEX, which can feed blocklists (stated by Shadowserver; not all are proven attackers).
watch_for: Detection rules for ARTEX traffic
Telecom intrusions attributed to agent tooling
Updates to the FBI ARTEX FLASH

direct: Deichmann says hackers accessed customer data in its online shop (names, addresses, invoices, emails, phones; no passwords or card numbers); Snipes, Ochsner Sport and Dosenbach are also affected per dpa and bluewin.
downstream: Customers in Germany, Austria and Switzerland are likely to get fake order and delivery messages before Black Friday (inference).
vanHaren reported the same data fields the same week; whether it is the same incident is not stated.
watch_for: A combined customer count
The cause (shop platform or supplier)
Phishing using Deichmann-group invoices

direct: ThreatDown says Booba ransomware started on an East Coast US water treatment plant's network and spread toward the local government that oversees it; it stopped it at the edge it monitored.
downstream: Where a utility and its municipality share networks but not monitoring, an attack crosses unseen (stated by ThreatDown as the lesson).
Other small utilities with outsourced IT may face the same ransomware (inference).
watch_for: The utility named or an EPA or CISA notice
Booba indicators in other utilities
Any effect on water treatment

direct: Swiss carrier Planzer says delivery data and customer-portal credentials (encrypted) were stolen; Digitec Galaxus says its customers' parcel numbers, names, addresses, emails and some phone numbers were affected, though its own systems were not.
downstream: Delivery-notice phishing in Switzerland during peak parcel season (inference).
Other shippers' customers of Planzer may be affected; none named yet.
watch_for: Other retailers naming Planzer
Planzer portal password resets
Parcel-tracking phishing
